policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'We must work the works of him that sent me' has the first-person plural subject of the base reading; RP's Eme would give 'I must work'.
ASV 'anointed his eyes with the clay' renders epechrisen; epetheken would be 'put/laid the clay upon his eyes'.
ASV supplies an un-italicized possessive in 'his eyes'; the base reading has the pronoun autou, the omission does not.
ASV reads 'his eyes'; the RP expansion tou tuphlou would be rendered 'the eyes of the blind man', which the ASV does not have.
ASV 'that he was a beggar' renders prosaites; RP's tuphlos would be 'that he was blind'.

ASV 'others said, No, but he is like him' has the negation and adversative of the base/WH text, excluding RP's de hoti, which lacks them. Base and r01 differ only in punctuation, which the English cannot distinguish.
ASV renders two connectives, 'They said therefore' for the elegon oun of the clause and 'How then' for the added oun; the base reading supplies only one.
ASV 'He answered, The man...' has no second verb of speaking; RP's kai eipen would give 'answered and said'.
ASV's definite 'The man that is called Jesus' renders the articular ho anthropos ho legomenos; the anarthrous RP reading would give 'A man called Jesus'.
Recitative hoti before direct speech is not rendered in English; ASV 'said unto me, Go to Siloam' is identical under either reading.
ASV 'Go to Siloam' names no pool; RP's ten kolumbethran tou would be rendered 'to the pool of Siloam'.
ASV's inferential 'so I went away and washed' renders oun; de would be the bare copulative 'and'.
ASV 'And they said unto him' has the copulative kai and no inferential; RP's Eipon oun would be 'They said therefore'.
ASV 'on the day when Jesus made the clay' renders the full relative phrase en he hemera; RP's hote would be simply 'when'.

The readings differ only in Greek word order and the article with theou; ASV 'This man is not from God' follows obligatory English order and renders no article, so the English does not distinguish them.
ASV's adversative 'But others said' renders the added de; the base reading is asyndetic.
ASV 'They say therefore unto the blind man' renders oun, which the RP omission lacks.
The readings differ only in the order of ti and su; ASV 'What sayest thou of him' follows fixed English interrogative order under either.
The readings differ only in the order of en and tuphlos; ASV 'that he had been blind' is identical under either.
ASV 'the parents of him that had received his sight' renders tou anablepsantos, which the omission lacks.
The readings differ only in the order of blepei and arti; ASV 'how then doth he now see?' is identical under either.
ASV 'His parents answered and said' has no indirect object; RP's de autois would add 'unto them'.

ASV 'ask him; he is of age' has the clause order of the base/WH text, excluding RP, which puts 'he is of age' first and adds autos. Base and r01 differ only in punctuation, which the English cannot distinguish.
eperotesate and erotesate are both rendered 'ask'; ASV 'ask him' does not distinguish the compound from the simple verb.
The readings differ only in the order of ton anthropon and ek deuterou; ASV 'called a second time the man that was blind' contains both elements and its English order settles neither.
The readings differ only in the position of houtos; ASV 'this man is a sinner' is identical under either.
ASV 'He therefore answered, Whether he is a sinner' has no second verb of speaking; RP's kai eipen would give 'answered and said'.
ASV 'They said therefore unto him' renders oun and has no 'again'; RP reads de and adds palin.

ASV 'And they reviled him' opens with a connective, which the asyndetic base reading does not supply; kai and hoi de are both rendered 'and they' in the ASV, so the English does not choose between them.
The readings differ only in the order of mathetes and ei; ASV 'Thou art his disciple' is identical under either.
ASV's definite 'herein is the marvel' renders the article to with thaumaston; the anarthrous RP reading yields 'a marvellous thing'.
ASV 'We know that God heareth not sinners' opens without a connective; the added de would be rendered 'Now we know'.
The readings differ only in the order of hamartolon and ho theos; ASV 'God heareth not sinners' follows obligatory English order under either.
The variant is the article with Iesous, which English does not render; ASV 'Jesus heard' is identical under either.
ASV 'and finding him, he said, Dost thou believe' has no indirect object; the added auto would be rendered 'said unto him'.
ASV text reads 'the Son of God' (theou) and relegates anthropou to the mapped textual_variant note, 'Many ancient authorities read the Son of Man.'
ASV 'Jesus said unto him' opens without a connective; the added de would be rendered 'And Jesus said unto him'.
ASV 'Those of the Pharisees who were with him heard these things' opens without a connective; RP's Kai would be rendered 'And'.
The readings differ only in the order of ontes and met' autou; ASV 'who were with him' is identical under either.
ASV 'your sin remaineth' has no inferential particle in the clause; the added oun would be rendered 'therefore'.
